::: {#exr-taylor}
## Taylor polynomials of the exponential function

The second series from @exr-radius is $e^x$. Its partial sums are the Taylor polynomials
$$
  T_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{x^k}{k!}.
$$

1. Implement the function `taylor_exp(x, n)`, which returns $T_n(x)$.

1. Compute the errors of $T_1(1), \ldots, T_{15}(1)$. How does the error fall?

::: {.lm-scaffold}
```{julia}
# function taylor_exp(x, n)
#     ...
# end
```
:::

::: {.lm-solution}
The function is in `src/taylor_exp.jl` (see the appendix).

```{julia}
ns = 1:15
[ns abs.(taylor_exp.(1.0, ns) .- exp(1.0))]
```

The error is about $1 / (n + 1)!$, the first term left out. It falls faster and faster; after about $17$ terms, it
reaches the level of the rounding errors.
:::
:::
